Fix an even integer $p\ge4$ and a primitive $2p$-th root of unity $A\in\mathbb C$. Put

$$
\zeta=A^2,\qquad q=-\zeta,\qquad r=p/2,\qquad
\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}=q+q^{-1}.
$$

The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$
[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.
$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$
\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.
$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, it also satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),$$

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

Work over $\mathbb C$ with a fixed loop parameter $\delta$. Let $\mathcal T_\delta$ be the strict Temperley–Lieb diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]: its objects are $n\in\mathbb N$, and its morphism space $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n)$ is the complex span of the noncrossing matching diagrams with $m$ bottom and $n$ top boundary points, composed by stacking and loop removal.

For a basis endomorphism $D:n\to n$, let $c(D)$ be the number of components after joining each top point to the corresponding bottom point outside the rectangle. Define the unnormalized closure trace by
$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)},$$
and extend linearly. This definition is valid for every $\delta\in\mathbb C$, including $\delta=0$.

For $m,n\in\mathbb N$, the subspace of **negligible morphisms** is
$$\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)= \{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n): \operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0\text{ for every }g\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(n,m)\}.$$
This definition specifies subspaces only. Their closure under composition and tensor product, and hence the quotient category, are supplied separately.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

Work over $\mathbb C$ with a fixed loop parameter $\delta$. Let $\mathcal T_\delta$ be the strict Temperley–Lieb diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]: its objects are $n\in\mathbb N$, and its morphism space $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n)$ is the complex span of the noncrossing matching diagrams with $m$ bottom and $n$ top boundary points, composed by stacking and loop removal.

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)},$$
and extend linearly. This definition is valid for every $\delta\in\mathbb C$, including $\delta=0$.

This definition specifies subspaces only. Their closure under composition and tensor product, and hence the quotient category, are supplied separately.

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, it also satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),$$

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

Use all $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Put $V=\Delta(1)$ and let $P_0$ be its trivial-channel projector in $V\otimes V=\Delta(2)\oplus\Delta(0)$. The maps

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}),\qquad U_i\longmapsto\delta P_{0,i,i+1}$$

are well defined. Their composite with the negligible quotient has kernel exactly the embedded boundary ideal $I_n=(p_{\ell-1})$ and induces

$$\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)/I_n\ \cong\ \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}).$$

Equivalently the target is the full centralizer on a chosen sum of the retained tilting summands. The unreduced map does **not** kill $p_{\ell-1}$: its image is the nonzero simple $\Delta(\ell-1)$.

The precise categorical comparison is with the additive Karoubi negligible quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$, equipped with its ordinary diagram braiding $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ and with planar pivotal structure multiplied by tensor parity $(-1)^n$. This is ribbon-equivalent to $\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell$. Its endomorphism algebras are identified with positive-loop TL algebras by $U_i=-e_i$. Its pivotal dimensions are $[a+1]_q$, and its twists on retained labels are $s^{a(a+2)}$. The quantum self-duality cup/cap have loop $-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$, whereas the parity-corrected pivotal closure has value $+\delta$ on $V$. Thus no equivalence of the unmodified positive-loop unoriented **pivotal** TL category is asserted.

On the highest-weight-$2$ and trivial prequotient channels, the quantum crossing eigenvalues are $s,-s^{-3}$; the Hecke element $T_i=qU_i-1=-s c_i^{-1}$ has eigenvalues $-1,q^2$. Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. Put

$$\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)=\{x\in\mathrm{TL}_n:\tau_n(xy)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathrm{TL}_n\}.$$

The additive idempotent-complete negligible quotient has simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$, represented by $p_a$, and

$$a\otimes b\cong\bigoplus_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}c.$$

At $n=\ell-1$ the unreduced algebra is semisimple, while its trace radical is the nonzero one-dimensional block generated by $p_{\ell-1}$. Trace radical and Jacobson radical are therefore distinct at this first boundary.

derivations.claim: By the boundary-projector result, $p_{r-1}$ is an idempotent with trace zero. The diagram category [F2] supplies the endomorphism algebra $\mathrm{TL}_{r-1}$ and its closure trace. For any $g\in\mathrm{TL}_{r-1}$, [F6] gives $p_{r-1}gp_{r-1}=\lambda p_{r-1}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$. Cyclicity [F5] gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{r-1}(g\circ p_{r-1})=\operatorname{Tr}_{r-1}(p_{r-1}gp_{r-1})=\lambda\operatorname{Tr}_{r-1}(p_{r-1})=0$. Thus $p_{r-1}$ itself is negligible by [F3].
By [F4], the negligible morphisms form a tensor ideal. Since [F3] and step 1.1 place $p_{r-1}$ in that ideal, the tensor ideal it generates is contained in the negligible ideal.

Put $A_0=e^{\pi i/(2r)}$. For $r\ge3$, $A_0$ is a primitive $4r$-th root, $q_0=A_0^2=e^{\pi i/r}$, and $-A_0^2-A_0^{-2}=-(q_0+q_0^{-1})$. Thus the negative-loop category in [F7] is exactly the BHMV Temperley–Lieb category at $A_0$; its quotient kernel is the ideal generated by $p_{r-1}$, and [F8] gives the complete label list.

If $r=2$, the loop value is zero and $p_1=1_1$ has zero trace by step 1.1. The tensor ideal it generates contains every identity $1_n$ for $n\ge1$, while the object $0$ has endomorphism algebra $\mathbb C$ with trace $1$. Hence the quotient is equivalent to finite-dimensional vector spaces with the single simple label $0$; its negligible ideal is exactly the ideal generated by $p_1$.

For arbitrary primitive $A$, write $A=A_0^k$ with $\gcd(k,4r)=1$. The cyclotomic automorphism $\sigma_k$ of $\mathbb Q(A_0)$ sends $A_0$ to $A$, sends $\delta(A_0)$ to $\delta(A)$, and sends every coefficient of each recursively defined projector and every closure-trace pairing matrix to its specialized coefficient at $A$. For each fixed pair of object labels, the matching set is finite by [F2], so the Hom spaces and trace-pairing matrices are finite-dimensional. The field automorphism preserves the ranks and kernels of all these matrices, the exact boundary ideal, and the quotient's simple labels. This completes the canonical-to-arbitrary-root transport and the proof.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
